text:
incident-bot: ❗ HIGH-SEVERITY: Dedicated pool 'odonex-prod' (tenant: Odonex) at 98% GPU utilization across 8 GPUs for 14m; 502 errors up to 3.9% on /v1/generate. Auto-escalating page to oncall. Runbook: https://wiki.redwood/prod/incidents/dedicated-pool

maya: oncall (sre) taking this. I'm pulling live dashboards and the tenant config. Acked.

liam (eng-runtime): autoscaler logs show scale decision suppressed due to pool flag `enterprise_pin=true`. No overflow allowed. Incoming QPS went from ~9k -> ~16k since 02:58 UTC. Queue depth trending to 800.

samir (eng-ops): confirmed pool config: `max_gpus=8`, `enterprise_pin=true`, `burst_policy=requires_approval`. Shared elastic pool has spare capacity: shared-elastic shows 6 GPUs idle.

alyssa (customer-success): Odonex reporting timeouts on their billing and analytics endpoints; they're on enterprise SLA (SLA-1). They're already paging their internal ops. High customer impact.

maya: options on the table:
- Request emergency burst to shared-elastic (fastest, cross-tenant contention risk)
- Soft-evict internal low-priority batch jobs inside odonex-prod (protect external endpoints but drop internal jobs)
- Route a portion of traffic to a smaller model for write-heavy endpoints (reduce mem/latency)
- Contact customer to throttle nonessential traffic while we remediate

liam (eng-runtime): quickest technical path is emergency burst + immediate 10% canary shift to a smaller variant for the hottest routes. I'll prepare the control-plane POST and related canary config.

maya: do not execute without infra approval. I'll page infra-leads: @darren @tonya. Include exact request payload.

liam (eng-runtime): POST payload prepared:
```
POST /controlplane/v1/pools/odonex-prod/actions
{
  "action": "enable_burst",
  "target_pool": "shared-elastic",
  "duration": "00:30:00",
  "requested_by": "liam",
  "reason": "tenant GPU exhaustion impacting SLA-1 customer"
}
```

incident-bot: Approval workflow #BR-8842 created; infra-lead approval required.

darren (infra-lead): I give emergency approval for 30m burst to shared-elastic. Proceed and monitor eviction impact. :ok_hand:

tonya (infra-lead): Approving as well. Keep burst to 30m and ensure we have traces for any cross-tenant errors.

samir (eng-ops): applying burst now. Changing `enterprise_pin` to false temporarily and attaching shared-elastic to routing. Patch applied at 03:12 UTC.

eng-ops: routing change live. Observed immediate routing delta: 40% of new sessions eligible for shared-elastic fallthrough. Evictions: expected low-priority jobs popped (about 900 jobs). Notifying tenants.

maya: starting 10% canary to `gpt-lite-1` on billing endpoints to reduce GPU memory pressure. Canary started at 03:14 UTC.

alyssa (customer-success): letting Odonex know: "We've invoked emergency capacity and started mitigating traffic; expecting reduced timeouts within minutes. We'll follow up with RCA." Customer replied: "Appreciate the quick response. Please keep us in loop."

liam (eng-runtime): 5m after burst: combined GPUs now 10/14 (after joining 4 GPUs from shared-elastic), avg p95 latency down from 3.6s -> 1.4s, 502s down to 1.2%. Queue depth dropped from 780 -> 90. Good recovery signal.

samir (eng-ops): tail error traces show main cause was prolonged KV cache pressure on bigger model variant under high concurrency. Canary shows smaller model reduces mem use and p95.

maya: expand canary to 25% for 10m. If stable, plan full variant shift to 50% for non-critical routes.

liam (eng-runtime): canary expanded. I'll capture trace ids and save sampling: traces: tx-7a9d, tx-7ac2, tx-7b01 (logged).

darren: note for postmortem: check why auto-approval path isn't available for SLA-1 customers. Suggest runbook update and automated one-click approval for infra leads.

samir (eng-ops): monitoring shared-elastic for eviction churn. We saw ~1.2k low-priority evictions; no high-priority tenant errors reported so far.

maya: monitoring period 15m. If errors remain <1% and latency stable, we'll end burst at approved time. Otherwise consider soft-eviction of internal batch tasks inside odonex-prod.

alyssa (customer-success): Odonex reports pages loading; decreased error rates on their side. They've asked for an RCA and whether credits will be issued under SLA. I'm collecting timelines.

eng-ops: at 03:40 UTC metrics: GPUs used 9/14, avg latency p95 ~1.2s, 502s 0.6%, queue 55. Recovery confirmed.

maya: good. Schedule the automatic revert at 03:42 UTC (end of 30m window). Assign action items:
- liam: own postmortem and RCA; include root cause (autoscaler suppression + model memory behavior) and recommend mitigations (policy changes, automated approvals, variant fallback).
- darren/tonya: review approval policy for SLA-1 customers, consider auto-approve TTL for oncall.
- eng-ops (samir): implement more verbose eviction notifications and tenant owner alerts automation.
- alyssa: draft customer-facing timeline and SLA credit calc.

samir (eng-ops): reverting temporary flags now; `enterprise_pin` set back to true and burst detached. Revert completed at 03:44 UTC. Final check: odonex-prod back to 8/8, avg utilization 66%, 502s <0.5%.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: BR-8842 closed. Summary: emergency burst to shared-elastic for 30m; canary variant shift reduced memory pressure; customer service restored. Closed at 03:46 UTC.

maya: thanks team. Quick postmortem sync in #postmortems in 45m. :white_check_mark:
